A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Causal-Adapter work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and expanded sections.

before.justification: v4 reports original Causal-Adapter results on Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI, and CelebA-HQ, alongside ablations, generated images, and causal-discovery experiments.

after.justification: v6 retains those original results and adds foundation-model comparisons, a human-body image study, and further causal-graph ablations.

M1.justification: The adapter, SCM, PAI, CTC, optional attention guidance, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Learnable adjacency with acyclicity regularization and the SD3/FlowEdit adaptation already appeared in v4 Appendices G and E.4. v6 provides additional implementation detail without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E.7 adds human-body images with greater pose, background, scale, and composition variation for age, gender, and beard editing without an SCM. This is a focused extension of human-image editing coverage; the four original datasets and their tasks remain.

E2.justification: v6 substantially expands the evaluated comparator set. Qwen-Image-Edit and Nano Banana 2 appear in Pendulum and ADNI qualitative comparisons; these models plus Flux.1-Kontext-Dev appear in CelebA and human-body comparisons (Tables 16–17, Figures 36–39). The original benchmark and causal-discovery comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include classifier accuracy and LPIPS on a CelebA subset, incorrect-graph controls, and a study using 100 manually annotated human-body images without an SCM. The original benchmark protocols remain. The new CelebA subset size and selection procedure, and the human-body training/evaluation split, are unspecified.

E4.justification: v6 adds explicit incorrect-graph tests on Pendulum and ADNI, with numerical and visual evidence about intervention propagation (Tables 5, 18–19; Figures 11, 42–43). These substantially extend v4's Pendulum known/no-mechanism/ground-truth comparison. Appendix E.7 also examines editing beyond aligned images; the earlier regularizer, guidance, compositional, and discovery analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report CelebA means and standard deviations over three random seeds in the corresponding identity-preservation table (v4 Table 12; v6 Table 13), and retain ADNI standard deviations. The added tables introduce no new run-count information, uncertainty estimation, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in the foundation-model comparisons and graph ablations. On the new CelebA subset, Causal-Adapter reports age-intervention accuracy of 72 versus Qwen's 62, but bald-intervention accuracy of 40 versus 94 for Qwen and Nano Banana 2. Original benchmark scores remain unchanged; v6 Tables 5/18 reuse v4's correct/no-mechanism Pendulum values while adding the incorrect-graph row.

T1.justification: The SCM definitions, Equations 1–8, and formal-identifiability qualifications remain unchanged. New Equation 9 explicitly instantiates the existing flow-matching-plus-CTC objective across SD3's three encoders; it adds no substantive derivation, theorem, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central method and performance claims, including the reported 91% Pendulum MAE and 87% ADNI FID reductions. Causal discovery was already claimed in v4 Appendix G; its greater main-text prominence does not constitute a new contribution.

C2.justification: v6 adds specific interpretations of correlation-driven edits and incorrect-graph propagation, and discusses foundation-model editing failures. Appendix E.7 explicitly limits the human-body findings to disentangled editing, disclaiming fully open-domain causal generation and identifying the need for richer annotations and causal knowledge. The existing identifiability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v6 adds a project-page link announcing access to code, training data, and models, absent from v4. Appendix E.4 also specifies SD3 encoder types, attribute-token allocation, per-encoder CTC, source/target conditioning, and 50 steps with guidance 1.5. New comparison prompts and human-data sourcing/annotation information further expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v6 adds Cao et al. (2025), CausalCtrl, to Appendix A and the references; it is cited rather than evaluated. The foundation-model studies extend empirical positioning against contemporary editors, while the existing novelty argument and broader related-work discussion remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the expanded graph discussion, rewritten SD3 explanation, and new Appendices E.6–E.7. Affiliations, publication information, acknowledgments, and the contents list are updated. Most existing prose, section organization, and the central narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v6 adds substantial comparison displays: foundation-model and human-body grids, graph-ablation figures, and corresponding tables. Figure 10 repackages existing Pendulum discovery panels from v4 Figures 34–35, while Table 5 repeats the appendix graph-ablation results. Most earlier figures are retained and renumbered, with some changes to face-image rendering.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly strengthens the paper through explicit graph-misspecification tests, broader baseline comparisons, and improved SD3 and resource-access documentation. These additions make applicability and reproducibility easier to assess. The gain is limited by incomplete specification of the new CelebA subset and human-body evaluation protocol, qualitative-only evidence for the latter, and mixed results in Tables 17 and 19 that limit broader performance conclusions.
